summary: Read-only research: NVIDIA Isaac Sim with ROS 2 Jazzy, MoveIt 2 driving an Isaac arm, Windows support, and what it means for testing ha-ros2-bridge

result.summary: Pin Isaac Sim 6.1.0 (GitHub tag 10 Sep 2026; docs updated 18 Sep 2026). Its ROS 2 bridge officially supports only Humble and Jazzy; Ubuntu 24.04 with Jazzy is NVIDIA's recommended pairing and matches ha-ros2-bridge. Isaac Sim cannot run on the Windows 10 PC: 6.x drops Windows 10, the container is Linux-only, WSL2 is unsupported for containers and deprecated for the bridge, and the PC's Pascal TITAN X has no RT cores and cannot reach the required 595 driver branch. Treat Isaac Sim as an integration tier on a separate Ubuntu 24.04 host (RT-core GPU, 16 GB VRAM) with the bridge node on the same host over Fast DDS. The Windows PC runs the MQTT-to-executor suite with a fake executor and MoveIt 2 on mock_components inside WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04. The executor should call MoveIt's /move_action from rclpy and map MoveItErrorCodes (31 values, success only when val == 1) to the bridge's result set.
result.isaac_jazzy_support:
VERSIONS (all checked 2026-10-13)
- GitHub tags: v5.0.0 8 Aug 2025; v5.1.0 21 Oct 2025; v6.0.0 4 Jun 2026; v6.0.1 22 Jun 2026; v6.1.0 10 Sep 2026 (marked Latest); v7.0.0a1 18 Sep 2026 (pre-release). NGC also shows a 6.2.0 container tag pushed 13 Oct 2026, but there is no GitHub tag and the 6.2.0 docs return 404, so 6.2.0 is not a GA release for planning purposes. The "latest" docs document 6.1.0 (download page: Isaac Sim 6.1.0, September 2026; last updated 18 Sep 2026). 5.1.0 docs carry the banner "no longer supported"; 4.5.0 docs pages return 404 (removal announced in the 6.0 GA forum post, 8 Jun 2026). Isaac Sim 6.x requires Python 3.12 (5.1 was Python 3.11 only).
- Decision input: pin Isaac Sim 6.1.0.

ROS 2 SUPPORT MATRIX (6.1 ROS 2 Installation page, docs "latest", accessed 2026-10-13)
- Ubuntu 24.04 + Jazzy: recommended, default Linux install, Python 3.12, system Jazzy can be sourced directly.
- Ubuntu 22.04 + Humble: default apt install (Python 3.10); custom interfaces need a Python 3.12 workspace built via NVIDIA's Docker build_ros.sh.
- Ubuntu 22.04 + Jazzy: build from source.
- Windows 11 + Jazzy via Pixi (native, rmw_zenoh_cpp by default, Zenoh router must run first; custom interfaces unsupported).
- Windows 11 + Humble or Jazzy via WSL2: Deprecated (custom interfaces unsupported; netsh port forwarding of 7400/7410/9387).
- "ROS 2 Humble on Ubuntu 24.04 is not an officially supported configuration." Windows 10 appears in no 6.x table. The 6.0 migration guide: Isaac Sim 6.0 "deprecates Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 (WSL2) and supports only Jazzy" on Windows.
- Experimental: 6.x can load any natively installed ROS 2 distro (Python 3.12 builds) but "Humble and Jazzy remain the officially tested and recommended distros". NVIDIA staff (forum, 16 Jan 2026): Kilted is not supported because Isaac Sim only supports LTS distributions. ROS 2 lifecycle (ros2_documentation Releases.rst): Jazzy EOL May 2029; Kilted EOL Dec 2026; Lyrical released 22 May 2026. isaacsim.ros2.core falls back to the Jazzy backend for an unsupported sourced distro; isaacsim.ros2.control (6.1) explicitly rejects unsupported distros.
- Conclusion: Jazzy on Ubuntu 24.04 is the only pairing that is simultaneously NVIDIA-recommended, matches the bridge's target, and shares Python 3.12 with Isaac Sim so the project workspace (including custom interfaces) can be sourced before launching Isaac Sim.

INTERNAL VERSUS SYSTEM ROS 2 LIBRARIES (6.1 docs)
- ROS_DISTRO decides: unset means the launchers (isaac-sim.sh, python.sh) auto-configure the bundled libraries (Humble on 22.04, Jazzy on 24.04 and Windows); if a ROS environment is sourced, the launcher preserves it; opt out with ./python.sh --no-ros-env (new in 6.1, isaacsim.ros2.core 1.11.0).
- FAQ: source a system ROS 2 or workspace only when you need custom messages, a non-default distro or a custom RMW. Internal libraries must be used when using ROS Docker containers or when only common interfaces (std_msgs, sensor_msgs, trajectory_msgs and so on) are needed.
- run_isaacsim.launch.xml argument use_internal_libs defaults true for Humble, false for Jazzy. On Windows the bridge extension is disabled by default; on Linux it is enabled via isaac.startup.ros_bridge_extension in apps/isaacsim.exp.full.kit.

RMW, FAST DDS PROFILE, DOMAIN ID (6.1 install_ros and FAQ)
- Linux launcher sets RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_fastrtps_cpp if unset. Single machine: default profile with shared-memory transport.
- Multi-machine or Docker: a UDPv4-only fastdds.xml (transport descriptor, participant profile, useBuiltinTransports false) saved as ~/.ros/fastdds.xml and exported as FASTRTPS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE before launching Isaac Sim and in every ROS 2 terminal and container.
- Cyclone DDS: Linux only (Humble and Jazzy), bundled with Python 3.12. Zenoh: Jazzy on Linux, no bundled libraries (build with Python 3.12), router required, default on Windows Pixi.
- ROS_DOMAIN_ID is optional but must match on every participant and be set before launching Isaac Sim; same RMW and same distro must be sourced on both sides. 6.1 adds Ros2ContextHandle.getDomainId. Topics are only published while the simulation is playing.

HEADLESS CONTAINER (install_container, 6.1.0; Dockerfile in isaac-sim/IsaacSim)
- nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-sim:6.1.0 (multi-arch, about 9.9 GB), base nvcr.io/nvidia/base/ubuntu:noble-20251013 (Ubuntu 24.04), ENTRYPOINT runheadless.sh, no ROS 2 apt packages. "The Isaac Sim container is supported only on Linux" and supports "Python apps and standalone examples in headless mode only".
- Run: --gpus all, -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y, --rm, --network=host, -u 1234:1234, eight cache/config/log volumes (chown or setfacl to 1234). Streaming ports 49100 TCP, 47998 UDP, 8210 TCP (Compose web viewer, Ubuntu hosts only); bridge-mode -p publishing does not work; no authentication or encryption on streaming endpoints.
- Jazzy bridge inside the 6.1 container: supported by composition (Ubuntu 24.04 base selects bundled Jazzy when ROS_DISTRO is unset; python.sh --headless scripts; ROS containers alongside with --net=host and the UDP Fast DDS profile), but no NVIDIA page walks through it explicitly, so the plan must start with a smoke test: press Play (or launch a standalone script) and run ros2 topic echo /clock from the bridge container.
- Alternative launch from the ROS side: ros2 launch isaacsim_bringup run_isaacsim.launch.xml ros_distro:=jazzy headless:=webrtc standalone:=<script> (Linux and Windows Pixi, not WSL2). Simulation Control services (enable with --/isaac/startup/ros_sim_control_extension=True; needs ros-jazzy-simulation-interfaces 1.5.0+): /set_simulation_state, /get_simulation_state, /step_simulation (paused only), /reset_simulation, /load_world, /spawn_entities, /get_entity_state and the /simulate_steps action, usable for deterministic setup and teardown.

LICENCE
- Apache 2.0 source plus NVIDIA Isaac Sim Additional Software and Materials License (v. 9 Jun 2025) for Kit and some assets. Licence FAQ: free for internal R&D with no per-seat limits; NVIDIA AI Enterprise licence needed only to redistribute Isaac Sim with Kit to third parties. Container requires ACCEPT_EULA=Y; pip path uses OMNI_KIT_ACCEPT_EULA. Not a blocker.
result.moveit_executor_path:
RECOMMENDED BINDING FOR THE EXECUTOR PLUGIN
- Use a plain rclpy action client on the MoveGroup action /move_action (moveit_msgs/action/MoveGroup) served by the move_group node. Capability names from moveit2 main capability_names.hpp (accessed 2026-10-13): move_action, execute_trajectory, plan_kinematic_path, compute_ik, compute_fk, check_state_validity, compute_cartesian_path, get_planning_scene, apply_planning_scene, query_planner_interface.
- Goal = MotionPlanRequest + PlanningOptions; result = error_code (MoveItErrorCodes), trajectory_start, planned_trajectory, executed_trajectory, planning_time; feedback = state string. With plan_only false, planning and execution failures arrive as one MoveItErrorCodes value, which keeps the bridge dependency set to rclpy plus moveit_msgs.
- Constraint: MotionPlanRequest (moveit_msgs ros2 branch) has no named-target field (fields are workspace_parameters, start_state, goal_constraints, path_constraints, trajectory_constraints, reference_trajectories, pipeline_id, planner_id, group_name, num_planning_attempts, allowed_planning_time, max_velocity_scaling_factor, max_acceleration_scaling_factor, cartesian_speed_limited_link, max_cartesian_speed, smoothness_level). The executor must therefore resolve a named pose to joint values itself (SRDF group_state entries, or a plugin-config YAML map) and send them as JointConstraints in goal_constraints. An unknown pose name is rejected by the plugin before any MoveIt call and never produces a MoveIt code.
- Alternatives recorded: (a) moveit_py (in the Jazzy moveit 2.12.4-1 release) gives PlanningComponent.set_goal_state(configuration_name=...) and named_target_states, but it is an in-process MoveItCpp that needs the full MoveIt parameter set and performs its own execution (MoveItPy.execute returns ExecutionStatus: UNKNOWN, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, PREEMPTED, TIMED_OUT, ABORTED, FAILED), so it is a second planning instance beside move_group; (b) C++ MoveGroupInterface.setNamedTarget/plan/move/execute return moveit::core::MoveItErrorCode but need a C++ node. Record the choice with its date.

HOW THE ARM IS DRIVEN IN ISAAC SIM (three tiers behind one xacro switch, ros2_control_hardware_type, as in NVIDIA's isaac_moveit package and the moveit_resources panda.ros2_control.xacro)
- Tier 1, Windows PC, no GPU: mock_components/GenericSystem. Covers the entire MQTT -> executor -> move_group -> error-code path.
- Tier 2, Isaac Sim classic bridge: OmniGraph ROS2 Publish Joint State and ROS2 Subscribe Joint State (sensor_msgs/JointState) on /isaac_joint_states and /isaac_joint_commands (renamed so they do not collide with joint_state_broadcaster's /joint_states), an external ros2_control_node, spawners joint_state_broadcaster and the arm joint_trajectory_controller, use_sim_time true. NVIDIA's jazzy_ws isaac_moveit (Franka, isaac_moveit.launch.xml) builds PickNik's topic_based_ros2_control from a vendored submodule; on Jazzy prefer the ros-controls binary topic_based_hardware_interfaces 1.1.0-1 (plugin joint_state_topic_hardware_interface/JointStateTopicSystem, same parameters joint_commands_topic, joint_states_topic, trigger_joint_command_threshold, sum_wrapped_joint_states, and an alias for the old plugin name since 1.1.0, 13 May 2026). Set sum_wrapped_joint_states true because Isaac reports joint positions wrapping between 2pi and -2pi. PickNik's topic_based_ros2_control has no Jazzy release and is flagged unmaintained on ROS Index.
- Tier 3, Isaac Sim 6.1 in-process ros2_control (isaacsim.ros2.control 0.1.6, Humble and Jazzy only, PhysX and Newton): the controller_manager runs inside Isaac Sim, configured by a ROS2ControlManager OmniGraph node (targetPrim, controllerConfig YAML, optional urdfPath, namespace, publishRobotDescription, useSimTime) or Ros2ControlManager.setup(prim_path, controller_config, ...). The URDF is synthesised from USD on each Play; command interface per joint is inferred from the drive (stiffness > 0 position, damping only velocity, no gains effort, no drive state only); no <hardware> block is written. Exposed: /joint_states, /robot_description (transient_local), /clock, <ns>/controller_manager and /<controller>/follow_joint_trajectory (control_msgs FollowJointTrajectory), which MoveIt's moveit_simple_controller_manager drives. NVIDIA-verified reference: UR10 with joint_state_broadcaster and scaled_joint_trajectory_controller (./python.sh standalone_examples/api/isaacsim.ros2.control/ur10_ros2_control_demo.py then ros2 launch isaac_ros2_control_demo ur10_in_process.launch.py; smoke test ros2_control_smoke_test.py --headless prints DEMO SMOKE TEST: PASS). Limitations: Stop tears down the controller_manager and Play recreates it, so controllers must be re-spawned after every Stop/Play; setup errors latch until Stop/Play; one ROS2ControlManager per articulation; update_rate clamped to physics rate.
- All Isaac tiers: use_sim_time true with /clock from ROS2 Publish Clock; topics exist only while playing; the executor must tolerate controllers being temporarily absent and a stalled /clock when the sim is paused.

MOVEITERRORCODES (moveit_msgs 2.6.0, the Jazzy release per ros/rosdistro jazzy/distribution.yaml; file fetched 2026-10-13 and identical on the ros2 branch). Fields: int32 val, string message, string source. Success only when val == 1. Values -8, -9 and -20 are unused.
Overall: SUCCESS 1; UNDEFINED 0; FAILURE 99999; PLANNING_FAILED -1; INVALID_MOTION_PLAN -2; MOTION_PLAN_INVALIDATED_BY_ENVIRONMENT_CHANGE -3; CONTROL_FAILED -4; UNABLE_TO_AQUIRE_SENSOR_DATA -5 (misspelling is in the source); TIMED_OUT -6; PREEMPTED -7.
Request errors: START_STATE_IN_COLLISION -10; START_STATE_VIOLATES_PATH_CONSTRAINTS -11; START_STATE_INVALID -26; GOAL_IN_COLLISION -12; GOAL_VIOLATES_PATH_CONSTRAINTS -13; GOAL_CONSTRAINTS_VIOLATED -14; GOAL_STATE_INVALID -27; UNRECOGNIZED_GOAL_TYPE -28; INVALID_GROUP_NAME -15; INVALID_GOAL_CONSTRAINTS -16; INVALID_ROBOT_STATE -17; INVALID_LINK_NAME -18; INVALID_OBJECT_NAME -19.
System errors: FRAME_TRANSFORM_FAILURE -21; COLLISION_CHECKING_UNAVAILABLE -22; ROBOT_STATE_STALE -23; SENSOR_INFO_STALE -24; COMMUNICATION_FAILURE -25; CRASH -29; ABORT -30.
Kinematics: NO_IK_SOLUTION -31.

MAPPING TO BRIDGE RESULT CODES (proposal; the project directory contained no result-code definition on 2026-10-13, so the target names below need Jonny's confirmation)
Proposed bridge set: SUCCEEDED, REJECTED, PLANNING_FAILED, EXECUTION_FAILED, TIMED_OUT, CANCELLED, UNAVAILABLE, INTERNAL_ERROR.
- 1 SUCCESS -> SUCCEEDED.
- -1, -2, -3, -31, -10, -11, -12, -13, -14 -> PLANNING_FAILED (keep the specific name in a reason field, for example goal_in_collision).
- -4 CONTROL_FAILED -> EXECUTION_FAILED.
- -6 TIMED_OUT -> TIMED_OUT.
- -7 PREEMPTED -> CANCELLED when the bridge itself sent cancel_goal, otherwise EXECUTION_FAILED (preempted by another client).
- -15, -16, -17, -18, -19, -26, -27, -28 -> REJECTED (malformed or unknown request content; same class as an unknown named pose, which the plugin rejects before calling MoveIt).
- -5, -22, -23, -24, -25 -> UNAVAILABLE (sensor, scene or communication not ready; retryable).
- -21, -29, -30, 0, 99999 and any value not in the table -> INTERNAL_ERROR.
- Action-server level failures that never yield a code: goal rejected by move_group, server absent (wait_for_server timeout), controllers missing after an Isaac Stop/Play -> UNAVAILABLE.
- If moveit_py is chosen instead, planning maps as above from MotionPlanResponse.error_code.val and execution maps from ExecutionStatus: SUCCEEDED -> SUCCEEDED, PREEMPTED -> CANCELLED or EXECUTION_FAILED, TIMED_OUT -> TIMED_OUT, ABORTED and FAILED -> EXECUTION_FAILED, UNKNOWN -> INTERNAL_ERROR.
- Always include the raw val and the message string in the MQTT result payload so Home Assistant automations can branch on the fine-grained code.

NEGATIVE TESTS THAT PROVOKE SPECIFIC CODES (run in Tier 1 first): unreachable pose -> -1 or -31; collision object at goal -> -12; start inside an obstacle -> -10; tiny allowed_planning_time -> -6; wrong group_name -> -15; unknown named pose -> plugin REJECTED, no code; cancel mid-motion -> -7; pause or stop Isaac Sim mid-trajectory (Tiers 2 and 3) -> -4 or, with moveit_py, ExecutionStatus ABORTED or TIMED_OUT. Known flaky case to exclude from bridge bugs: the Franka hand close goal can fail or abort on some machines (NVIDIA 6.1 MoveIt tutorial); NVIDIA's 6.0.1 page also noted intermittent timeouts on Humble and recommended Jazzy.

JAZZY VERSION PINS (ros/rosdistro jazzy/distribution.yaml, 2026-10-13): moveit 2.12.4-1 (includes moveit_py, moveit_ros_move_group, moveit_simple_controller_manager); moveit_msgs 2.6.0-1; ros2_control 4.49.0-1; ros2_controllers 4.43.0-1 (joint_trajectory_controller); topic_based_hardware_interfaces 1.1.0-1; no topic_based_ros2_control; no isaac_ros2_messages. ROS Index showed 2.15.2 and 2.7.2 for moveit and moveit_msgs, which appear to be Rolling values; the rosdistro file is authoritative for apt on Jazzy.
result.local_test_topology:
WHY ISAAC SIM IS DEFERRED FROM THE WINDOWS PC (no networking workaround changes this)
- Read-only hardware check on 2026-10-13 (Get-CimInstance): NVIDIA TITAN X (Pascal), driver 576.52, Windows 10 Pro build 19045, Intel i7-6850K (6 cores), 32 GB RAM; the card has 12 GB GDDR5X (2016 reviews; WMI shows the 4 GB cap). Pascal predates RT cores.
- Isaac Sim 6.x requirements (docs updated 18 Sep 2026, re-fetched 2026-10-13): "Windows 10 is not supported"; supported OS Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 or Windows 11; minimum GeForce RTX 4080 with 16 GB VRAM; tested drivers Linux 595.58.03 and Windows 595.97; "GPUs without RT Cores (A100, H100) are not supported". NVIDIA's Unix driver deprecation notice says the 580 series is the last to support Pascal, so this card cannot reach the 595 branch. 5.1.0 (now marked unsupported) still listed Windows 10 but with the same RTX 4080 minimum.
- No Linux-side escape on this PC either: NVIDIA staff (31 Oct 2025) state Isaac Sim containers are not supported under WSL2; the container is Linux-only; the 6.1 ROS 2 docs say the Docker workflow is not supported on Windows WSL2 and isaacsim_bringup does not support WSL2.
- Windows 10 WSL2 is NAT-only; mirrored networking with multicast needs Windows 11 22H2+ (Microsoft WSL networking doc, updated 2 Jun 2026). DDS multicast discovery does not cross the WSL2 NAT (NVIDIA staff, 23 Jun 2026; ROS Answers 385611). Docker Desktop host networking is layer 4 only, attaches to the Docker VM rather than the Windows LAN, and multicast reception is reported not to work (Docker docs; ROS Answers 416676; Docker forum). Local state observed: WSL 3.0.1.0 in NAT mode, distros Ubuntu-22.04 and Ubuntu 24.04.3 with no /opt/ros, Docker Desktop 4.41.1 installed but not running.

WHAT TO RUN ON THE WINDOWS PC (Tier 1, no GPU, runs today)
- Preferred: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 (already installed) with native ros-jazzy (apt), ros-jazzy-moveit (binary install documented for Ubuntu 24.04), the rclpy ha-ros2-bridge node, the fake executor plugin, the real MoveIt executor plugin against mock_components/GenericSystem via the shared xacro switch, and an MQTT broker. Everything that speaks DDS stays inside the one WSL2 distro, so only MQTT over TCP crosses to Home Assistant. Run headless; do not depend on RViz.
- Equivalent alternative: a docker compose project on Docker Desktop with ros:jazzy (Ubuntu noble; tags jazzy, jazzy-ros-core, jazzy-ros-base, jazzy-perception) containers plus a broker on a single Docker network. Never use Docker Desktop containers for DDS to anything outside that Docker network.
- Settings for the local suite: RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_fastrtps_cpp explicitly (matches Isaac Sim's Linux default), one ROS_DOMAIN_ID, and ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST (Jazzy dynamic discovery; not honoured by rmw_zenoh). Write the executor contract tests against the fake executor first; the Isaac stage re-runs the same contract tests against the real executor.
- Negative-code tests (planning failures, invalid group, timeouts, cancel) all run here against mock_components.

WHAT TO RUN ON THE UBUNTU MACHINE (Tiers 2 and 3)
- Isaac Sim 6.1.0 and the bridge node on the same host. Simplest: both native (default Fast DDS with shared memory). If the bridge is containerised: Isaac Sim container and bridge container both with --network=host, same ROS_DOMAIN_ID, same RMW, FASTRTPS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE pointing at the UDPv4-only fastdds.xml inside every container and terminal, set before Isaac Sim starts.
- First smoke test: launch headless, start playing, and confirm ros2 topic echo /clock from the bridge side before any arm test. Then Tier 3 UR10 ros2_control smoke test, then the project's own scene.
- Observation from the Windows PC: Isaac Sim WebRTC Streaming Client 2.0.0 (TCP 49100, UDP 47998) or the Compose web viewer on 8210, private network only, no authentication.

STRETCH ONLY, NOT IN THE BASELINE PLAN
- A Windows 10 Docker Desktop node speaking DDS to the remote Isaac host would need a Fast DDS Discovery Server (fastdds discovery --server-id 0 on UDP 11811; ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER and ROS_SUPER_CLIENT=TRUE on both sides; FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS=UDPv4) or rmw_zenoh in client mode towards a router (TCP 7447), neither of which NVIDIA documents for this topology, and Docker Desktop containers advertise unreachable internal IPs. Do not rely on netsh portproxy (TCP only per Microsoft, updated 20 Jan 2026) or on WSL2 mirrored mode (Windows 11 only).
- Any future Windows 11 Isaac host would speak Jazzy over rmw_zenoh_cpp (Pixi path), which does not interoperate with Fast DDS nodes or zenoh-bridge-ros2dds, so the bridge node would have to switch RMW. Not relevant to this PC, whose GPU rules Isaac Sim out regardless of OS.
requirements_for_isaac_machine: Operating system: Ubuntu 24.04 (NVIDIA's recommended pairing with ROS 2 Jazzy for Isaac Sim 6.1; docs updated 18 Sep 2026). Ubuntu 22.04 is possible but defaults to Humble and needs a Python 3.12 Jazzy build.

GPU with RT cores and at least 16 GB VRAM: minimum tier GeForce RTX 4080 16 GB; good tier RTX 5080 16 GB; ideal RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 48 GB. GPUs without RT cores (A100, H100) and all Pascal-era cards are unsupported. Data-centre guidance from the GitHub README: A40 minimum, L40S recommended. Ask Jonny which GPU and VRAM the Ubuntu machine has before scheduling Isaac tests.
CPU, RAM, disk: minimum Intel i7 7th gen or Ryzen 5 with 4 cores, 32 GB RAM, 50 GB SSD; good tier 8 cores, 64 GB RAM, 500 GB SSD (6.1 requirements table).

NVIDIA driver: Isaac Sim 6.1.0 was tested on Linux 595.58.03; NVIDIA recommends the Latest Production Branch for newer GPUs. If using the pip install path instead of the container, GLIBC 2.35+ is required.

Container route: Docker plus NVIDIA Container Toolkit; image nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-sim:6.1.0 (about 9.9 GB, headless only, Linux only); run with --gpus all, -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y, --network=host, -u 1234:1234 and the documented cache/config/log volumes chowned or setfacl'd to UID 1234. Expect a slow first launch while shaders cache and keep the cache volumes persistent.

ROS 2 Jazzy system install on Python 3.12 (ros-jazzy-desktop or ros-base) so the ha-ros2-bridge workspace and any custom interfaces can be sourced directly before launching Isaac Sim; or rely on Isaac Sim's bundled Jazzy libraries when only common interfaces are used.

MoveIt and control packages at the Jazzy rosdistro versions (2026-10-13): moveit 2.12.4 (ros-jazzy-moveit), moveit_msgs 2.6.0, ros2_control 4.49.0, ros2_controllers 4.43.0 (joint_trajectory_controller), topic_based_hardware_interfaces 1.1.0 for the Tier 2 topic-based path, ros-jazzy-simulation-interfaces 1.5.0+ for the Simulation Control services, and ros-jazzy-ur-moveit-config if the NVIDIA UR10 ros2_control demo is used as the Tier 3 reference.

NVIDIA IsaacSim-ros_workspaces jazzy_ws built with colcon: isaacsim_bringup (run_isaacsim.launch.xml), isaac_moveit (Franka, Tier 2 reference), isaac_ros2_control_demo (UR10, Tier 3 reference), isaac_tutorials (ros2_publisher.py test publisher).

DDS configuration: Fast DDS (rmw_fastrtps_cpp) on every participant; if anything runs in a container or on another machine, a UDPv4-only ~/.ros/fastdds.xml exported as FASTRTPS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE in every terminal and container before Isaac Sim starts; identical ROS_DOMAIN_ID everywhere; the same distro sourced on both sides.

Network: MQTT reachability from the bridge node to the Home Assistant broker; for remote viewing open TCP 49100 and UDP 47998 (WebRTC client) or TCP 8210 (Compose web viewer) to trusted addresses only, since the streaming endpoints have no authentication or encryption; only one streaming client per instance.

Licence and accounts: Isaac Sim is free for internal R&D with no seat limits (Licence FAQ); the container needs ACCEPT_EULA=Y; check once whether the NGC pull works anonymously or needs an NGC API key.

Simulation lifecycle tooling: enable isaacsim.ros2.sim_control (--/isaac/startup/ros_sim_control_extension=True) so tests can reset, pause, step and load worlds through services instead of GUI actions; plan for controllers to be re-spawned after every Stop/Play when using the in-process ros2_control path.

Fallback if no suitable local GPU exists: a cloud instance running the 6.1.0 container, for example NVIDIA Brev with 1x L40S via Docker Compose (ports 49100, 47998, 8210 restricted to your IP); budget from the provider's own pricing page.
unverified: Isaac Sim 6.2.0 as a GA release: only an NGC container tag (pushed 13 Oct 2026) exists; no GitHub tag, no release notes, docs URL returns 404.

Exact calendar years of the GitHub release tags: the releases page shows day and month; years were inferred from docs dates. The 6.1.0 release date of September 2026 comes from the download page and a third-party blog.

An explicit NVIDIA walkthrough of enabling the ROS 2 Jazzy bridge inside the nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-sim:6.x headless container: not found; expected to work by composition of documented pieces and must be smoke-tested (ros2 topic echo /clock).
Whether an anonymous docker pull of nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-sim:6.1.0 succeeds without an NGC API key.

Whether GPUs below the published minimum (8 to 12 GB VRAM) run a simple arm scene; NVIDIA staff only point to the requirements page. The 4.5-era minimum (RTX 3060 or 3070, 8 GB) is known only from forum snippets because the 4.5 docs now return 404.
Lyrical support in Isaac Sim: no source either way. Kilted being unsupported is sourced (NVIDIA staff, 16 Jan 2026).
Behaviour of ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY and CYCLONEDDS_URI with Isaac Sim: not mentioned in the Isaac Sim docs.

A Windows 10 Docker Desktop node reaching a remote Isaac Sim host through a Fast DDS Discovery Server: community guidance only; the NVIDIA forum thread closed without a confirmed fix and no staff reply covered that exact topology.
Whether Isaac Sim 5.1's bundled Humble Fast DDS honours ROS_SUPER_CLIENT (Humble's Fast DDS version not checked); moot for the 6.1 plan.
That netsh portproxy being TCP-only makes NVIDIA's documented UDP port forwarding (7400, 7410, 9387) ineffective: an inference from the Microsoft and NVIDIA pages, not a tested claim.
WSL2 IP address changing across restarts under NAT: community reports, not confirmed against Microsoft documentation.
Zenoh middleware via WSL2 on Windows: NVIDIA states it is untested; treat as not working until shown otherwise.
Humble-to-Jazzy cross-distro traffic for standard message types: one NVIDIA staff statement (23 Jun 2026); not an officially tested configuration.
Brev L40S pricing of about USD 2.69 per hour plus storage: community figure, not from Brev's pricing page.
